item.content:encoded:
I apologize for the necropost, but my thoughts exactly. I was raised in conservative Judaism and this story reminds me of many I studied as a child. religion — religions — the old classics, in fact — are already in this.

as an interesting aside, the word "apple" does not even once show up in the original texts of the story of the tree of knowledge (I don't believe the fruit is mentioned in this story, so this is kind of a non sequitur). there were no apples in that part of the middle east at that time. it was most likely a lemon. there you go, that's your Torah/Tanakh lesson for the day.

item.content:encoded:
What with Sunnclockworks's new article about Chinese snake people and the increased view of Mekhane and Yaldaboath as two snakes, with Mekhane becoming a cage and containing the flesh god, I had some ideas. Posting them here since this article is the most relevant to my points.

+ Some points
- which may be pointy

So in some stories, Mekhane is the cage for Yaldaboath, and they are both serpents, as Nahash the serpent is a serpent. So what happens if Mekhane is the library, and Yaldaboath is the serpent/ Nahash? Together they create/teach humanity as siblings, then after the actions of this story Mekhane becomes the Library and contains/protects her repentant brother. Some humans see this and misinterpret, becoming the Sarkists and the CotBG.

item.content:encoded:
Ok, so Cain and Able are, in fact, brothers, and they are also THAT Cain and Able. Before I read this, there were still doubts.
This also establishes that the Scarlet King and the Daevites are connected. That makes an ungodly amount of sense.
It's also established that 1) the Broken God is actually a Broken Goddess, 2) that she's the sister of the Serpent, 3) that the Serpent is THAT Serpent, and 4) the Serpent isn't a bad guy.

I know there's not technically a canon, but can someone tell me 1) is this universally accepted as canon, and 2) what other massive pieces of background story have been established that I don't know about?

I really want to know what took place before this tale. And after, and during but elsewhere.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The witness line was a reference to Steven Erikson's Book of the Fallen series (super awesome epic fantasy series go read them), which has a character named Karsa Orlong (who looks like this), who uses it as something of a catchphrase, usually before he's about to do something very, very impressive.

As you can see by the illustration, Karsa provides a pretty good model for Able to aspire to, re: gigantic god-slaying abattoir on legs, destroyer of civilization etc. I actually threw a quasi-reference to him in an earlier tale (Mud on the Carpet) - when Satan mentions that "any inbred barbarian with a magic sword can kill a god."

Qayin once more took up a stone to slay his brother, and for this Ab-Leshal tore off his arms, first the right, and then the left.

This line in particular sticks in my head. I just can't get over the image, nor the particular way you describe it.

One thing: when she's referred to as The Voice Who Spoke for God, the Tree of Knowledge's name changes spelling, and I've no idea which is correct.
